headline: Cartalax
punch: The least documented compound in its own family.

headline: What it actually is
body: Marketed as the cartilage-targeted member of the Khavinson bioregulator family, the synthetic analogue of the crude extract Sigumir. | Worth noting at the outset: the documented sequences for its relatives are clean, Epitalon is AEDG, Vilon is KE, Vesugen is KED, Livagen is KEDA. **Cartalax's sequence is ambiguous in the literature.** For a compound you would be dosing, that is an unusual starting position.
punch: Its own sequence is not settled.

headline: What it claims
body: The claimed mechanism is substantial: chondroprogenitor to chondrocyte transition, osteoblast reinforcement at the cartilage-bone interface, increased type I collagen, decreased MMP9, decreased TNF-α and IL-6, increased CD98HC and mTORC1 signalling, and increased paracrine IGF-1 alongside SIRT6. | An independent source, Linkova 2023, attributes its action to NF-κB, IGF1 and TNKS2 modulation in ageing MSCs, which at least partly corroborates the list.
punch: A long mechanism list with partial corroboration.

headline: One claim contradicts itself
body: Read two items on that list together. It claims increased **IGF-1** and increased **SIRT6** at the same time. | SIRT6 normally **restrains** IGF and growth signalling. Those two going up together is unusual and the source does not address why it is not self-cancelling. When a mechanism list contains its own brake, somebody needs to explain which one wins.
punch: The claimed mechanism includes its own off switch.

headline: Wrong control system
body: This is the objection that matters more than any dosing or purity question. Growth plate closure is **a hormonally timed developmental event driven by estradiol at the chondrocyte**. It is not a degenerative process. | A chondroprotective, anti-inflammatory peptide is built to slow degeneration. Even granting every claimed effect, it is operating on the wrong control system for the outcome people want from it.
punch: ==Closure is not degeneration. It is a timed program.==

headline: Twelve hits
body: Of Epitalon, Cartalax, Pinealon and Vesugen, Cartalax is **the least documented**, with **12 total Europe PMC hits**. Not 12 trials. Twelve records of any kind. | And the **human capsule peptide content has never been quantified in any source**, so the amount of peptide in a dose is not a known quantity either.
punch: Twelve records, and nobody has measured what is in the capsule.

headline: The literature is confused
body: One concrete example of how unreliable the source material is. A PDF circulating as *Pinealon (KED)* had **Pinealon and Vesugen transposed throughout its text**. | So claims attributed to Pinealon in that document, including an in-vitro optimum concentration, p53 findings and serotonin results, actually belong to Vesugen. If the documents mix up which peptide is which, claims sourced from them are not reliable at the compound level.
punch: Source documents have the compounds swapped.

headline: Potency is not transferable
body: Cartalax is the synthetic analogue of the crude extract Sigumir, and the two are not interchangeable by dose. There is roughly a **100-fold gap** between them, with about a 10-fold gap in vitro: 2000 ng/mL Sigumir against 200 ng/mL Cartalax. | The same pattern holds across the family. Epitalon is 100 to 1000 times more potent than Epithalamin, its crude parent. Doses quoted for one do not transfer to the other.
punch: Crude and synthetic are different drugs.

headline: The family problem
subhead: LIMIT · WHAT APPLIES TO ALL OF THEM
body: No peer-reviewed efficacy evidence outside a small Russian literature that has not been internationally replicated. Dosing figures not grounded in pharmacokinetic studies. | And **zero direct evidence in a growing animal or on craniofacial tissue** for any of Epitalon, Cartalax, Pinealon or Vesugen. Every claimed relevance is extrapolated from adult, aged or ovariectomised models.
punch: Zero data in anything that was still growing.

headline: It is still low risk
body: At 1 to 10 mg a day these peptides are expected to be hydrolysed into common dietary amino acids, which is why even sceptics rate the family as **low risk of harm**. | So the case against Cartalax is not that it will hurt you. It is that there is no coherent reason to expect it to do the specific thing it is sold for.
punch: The objection is efficacy, not safety.

headline: Verdict
body: The weakest-documented compound in a family with a disputed mechanism, with an ambiguous sequence, unquantified capsule content, a self-contradictory mechanism claim, and source documents that confuse it with its relatives. | And the structural objection stands regardless of all that: it targets degeneration, and growth plate closure is a timed developmental programme, not degeneration.
punch: No. And not for a close reason.
